ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state organic structure, containing a free NC⁻ at the upper left, and on the left there is also an NC group connected to the skeleton; above there is a cyclopropanone/carbonyl part, and multiple curved arrows are also drawn in the figure; in the main skeleton, a C–Br bond, several C–C single bonds, one C=C double bond, and several methyl/side-chain connections can be seen. Curved arrows are not counted as bonds. Reasoning: According to the specified method, every connection between non-hydrogen atoms is counted as 1 bond, and double bonds and triple bonds are also each counted as one connection. The free NC⁻ at the upper left has 1 N–C bond. The NC group connected to the skeleton on the left has 2 bonds: an N–C bond and a C–skeleton bond. The top cyclopropanone/carbonyl part has 4 bonds: C=O, the 2 C–C bonds from the carbonyl carbon to the two top ring carbons, and the C–C bond between the two top ring carbons. The remaining visible non-hydrogen connections of the main skeleton, including the left/lower ring skeleton, the C–Br bond, methyl/side-chain bonds, the right ring skeleton, and one C=C connection, total 14 bonds. Therefore the total number is 1 + 2 + 4 + 14 = 21.
